summary:
40/40 rows adjudicated against the primary sources; every one of the 13 cited papers was available locally in /home/user/oligos/sources/cns/ (11 PMC JATS files plus the Kuroda supplement PDF), so nothing was UNVERIFIABLE. Verdicts: 4 CONFIRMED, 31 CONFIRMED_MINOR, 5 REFUTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE. Severity: 0 critical, 9 major, 27 minor, 4 none. Convention used: REFUTED is reserved for rows where the cited locus does not support the claim (silence-based grade 0, wrong dose, wrong delivery route). Rows where the number and locus are right but the grade is not rubric-defensible, or a comparator/sign is ambiguous, are CONFIRMED_MINOR with severity major and an explicit correction. 

The 5 REFUTED rows: CMS2102 (PPP2R5D NSC arm), CMS2111 (KCNT1 free-uptake dose range) and CMS2123 (Kuijper HTT-AON cell death) are grade-0 rows resting on silence rather than measurement. CMS2105 (SMA organoid) records delivery_method=intraparenchymal for a morpholino that Methods say was 'added directly to each well' - it is gymnotic free uptake. CMS2156 (sbASO BLOCK-iT control) records dose 250 nM when the source says 'no cell death observed at concentrations BELOW 250 nM' - the row asserts a negative at exactly the concentration the paper excludes. 

EFFICACY MISFILED AS TOXICITY: none found. This lane handled the trap well. Every knockdown/rescue row is graded 0 - the PPP2R5D neurite rescue (CMS2099), the KIF1A neurite rescue (CMS2108) and the SMA organoid firing-rate normalisation (CMS2105) are all correctly recorded as benefit, not hazard. CMS2105 in particular could easily have been misread: an INCREASE in neuronal firing looks like excitotoxicity until you check Fig 4b,c, where SMA organoids are hypo-active vs control (1.355 vs 1.956 Hz), making the treated 1.843 Hz a normalisation. The extractor got that right. Two rows do inflate the high-priority chronic bucket with what are really efficacy or acute endpoints (CMS2108 - a pure disease-phenotype rescue filed as chronic_neurotoxicity/high_chronic_neurotox; CMS2078 - a 3-hour transfection readout filed as chronic_neurotoxicity), but neither records efficacy as a toxicity signal. 

GRADE-0 ROWS RESTING ON SILENCE: three, all in the same shape - the source_table points at a Methods dosing sentence, readout_value/effect_direction/effect_vs_control are TBD, and the grade-0 comes from the paper not having mentioned harm. CMS2102 (PPP2R5D E198K NSCs, 10 uM, 72 h): the only result reported for that arm is an efficacy negative (no significant knockdown, attributed to ASO dilution in proliferating cells); the Fig 2D/2E it cites are baseline untreated-genotype proliferation comparisons. CMS2111 (KCNT1 KT777ps, 0.3-10 uM free uptake): the Methods sentence is quoted accurately but reports no outcome - and the same paper contains two properly-sourced measured negatives for KT777 that should have been used instead (Fig 1g/Suppl Table 5: only 11 additional downregulated genes beyond KCNT1 after 2 weeks gymnotic 10 uM in human iPSC neurons; Extended Data Fig 2e-g: normal neurite morphology at 3 weeks). CMS2123 (Kuijper HTT-AON): the paper reports cell death for the ATXN3-AON only and never states an HTT-AON negative; the row's own effect_vs_control says 'no cell death reported', which concedes the point. The same paper does supply an explicit measured negative for ATXN3-AON2 ('For ATXN3-AON2, no cell death was observed') that would make a legitimate grade-0 row. 

PPP2R5D MEAN/MEDIAN CONFLICT - RESOLVED. Both statistics are in the fetched paper: the Results text reports means, the Fig 5E/5H legends report the plotted medians. The three neurite rows in MY batch all survive the median reading: CMS2090 scramble (mean 60.78 vs untreated 59.04; medians 56.1 vs 55 - no change either way), CMS2093 ASO267 (mean 62.68; medians 57.9 vs 56.1 - no change either way), CMS2099 ASO249 at DIV35 (mean 127.1 vs corrected control 123.9; medians 115.3 vs 108.3 - still above the corrected control, so still a rescue). The row that flips is an ASO243 neurite row, which is NOT in my 40 but exists in the wider set. ASO243 is the only arm whose mean and median disagree materially, and it disagrees at BOTH timepoints and in the same direction: DIV11 mean 54.78 vs corE198K 49.33 (above control, reads as partial rescue) but median 29.8 vs corE198K 45.3 (34% BELOW the healthy control); DIV35 mean 126.9 vs corE198K 123.9 (above control, the paper's 'complete rescue') but median 102.7 vs corE198K 108.3 (below control). The mean-minus-median gap for ASO243 is ~25 um at both timepoints against ~4-6 um for every other arm, i.e. a uniquely skewed or bimodal distribution - which is itself a neurite-retraction signature in a subpopulation. Under a median reading, ASO243 does not normalise neurite length; it shortens neurites below the CRISPR-corrected control, which is a toxicity signal (grade 1-2), not a grade-0 rescue. I cannot adjudicate which statistic is correct without the per-neurite source data, and the authors plot medians while arguing entirely from means. RECOMMENDATION: any ASO243 neurite-outgrowth row must carry both statistics, cite the Results text (not Fig 5E/5H) as the source of the mean, and be marked disputed/grade_provisional - it must not be filed as a clean grade-0 rescue. 

DELIVERY MODE (check 3): verified individually for all 40. Correct everywhere except CMS2105 (see above). Free-uptake claims all check out - SCA3 5 uM 'added to the supernatant... do not need transfection procedures'; PPP2R5D 'gymnotic uptake at a 10 uM final concentration'; KIF1A '10 uM to be incorporated via gymnosis'; MECP2 'ASOs were added directly to the media'; Kotowska-Zimmer '2 uM added into the culturing media'; microglia 'unfacilitated free delivery'. Forced-delivery rows are also correctly labelled: Kuroda (Lipofectamine 2000), Kuijper (0.3% Lipofectamine 2000, 200 nM, 4 h), sbASO (Lipofectamine 3000), van Roon-Mom (Lipofectamine 2000, 500 nM). One exposure-design correction: the PPP2R5D notes describe '4 weeks of continuous exposure', but Methods specify a single 10 uM bolus at DIV3 followed by half-medium changes three times a week - progressive washout, not continuous dosing. That materially weakens the 'selectivity degrades under chronic exposure' framing on CMS2087/CMS2096. 

CELL MODEL HONESTY (check 4): clean. No neuroblastoma line is dressed up as an iPSC neuron. BE(2)-M17 and SH-SY5Y rows say so; hiPSC rows name the donor/patient line (AX2, C1.1, C2, ND42223, E198K, P305L, R474H); the Kuijper C1.1/C2 lines are correctly not claimed as patient-derived (the paper calls them control iPSCs); the van Roon-Mom row correctly says neuron/astrocyte coculture; CMS2147 is correctly marked species=rat. Only nit: CMS2147 says 'cortical', which the paper does not state ('rat primary neuron cultures'). 

ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY FLAGGING (check 5): both MEA/activity rows are correct. CMS2105 and CMS2147 both carry readout_category=electrophysiology and challenge_priority=low_acute_electrophysiology, so the brief's deprioritised material is filterable in one predicate as the schema intends. 

PREPRINTS (check 6): none. All 13 sources are peer-reviewed journal articles with PMC records and explicit licence statements (Mol Neurodegener, Biomedicines, Hum Mol Genet x2, RNA, HGG Advances, Mol Ther Nucleic Acids x3, Nat Commun x2, Nat Med, Nucleic Acid Therapeutics). No row needs redistribution=verify.
systematic_issues:
1. REDISTRIBUTION SYSTEMATICALLY UNDER-CLAIMED - 29 of 40 rows (73%). Every row in this batch carries redistribution=summary_stat, but 7 of the 13 source papers are CC BY 4.0 and should be cc_by: Kuroda 2025 (8 rows), Kuijper 2025 (6 rows), PPP2R5D 2025 (6 rows), microglia 2024 (5 rows), Kotowska-Zimmer 2021 (2 rows), MECP2-duplication 2024 (1 row), van Roon-Mom 2024 (1 row). The remaining 11 rows are correctly summary_stat (CC BY-NC-ND: SCA3 2022, SMA organoid 2025, KIF1A 2026, AD multigene 2026, KCNT1 2026; CC BY-NC: sbASO 2024). This is the mirror image of the over-claim the brief warns about and is not cosmetic: the schema tracks cc_by separately because it is what permits whole per-oligo panels to be republished verbatim with attribution. Flattening it forfeits that right across most of the lane. Fix mechanically: read the <license> element of each PMC record rather than defaulting to summary_stat. Expect the same ~70% under-claim across the ~80 in vitro rows outside this sample, since open-access CC BY dominates this literature. 

2. GRADE-0 FROM SILENCE - 3 of 40 (7.5%), and the pattern is mechanically detectable. Every instance has the same fingerprint: source_table names a Methods section rather than a figure or table, AND readout_value/effect_direction/effect_vs_control are all TBD, AND neurotox_grade=0. Run that predicate over the full in vitro set and quarantine every hit - I would expect ~6 more among the unchecked ~80. A rule worth adopting: a grade-0 row must cite a figure, table or a Results sentence that reports an outcome; a Methods dosing sentence can never support one. Two of the three were avoidable - the KCNT1 and Kuijper papers both contained properly-sourced measured negatives elsewhere that the extractor walked past. The extractor did flag two of the three as 'Weak row - flagged', so the judgement was partly right; the fix is to drop rather than downgrade. 

3. COMPARATOR AMBIGUITY IN MITIGATION-STUDY ROWS - 5 of 8 Kuroda rows, and this will recur in any SAR/chemistry-optimisation paper. In these papers the meaningful comparator is the toxic parent oligo, but readout_unit is '% of vehicle'. The result is rows where effect_direction is measured against the parent while the unit points at vehicle. On CMS2072 (LDH, decrease) and CMS2075 (cell_number, increase) this inverts the sign relative to the declared unit: both read as protective/benign against vehicle, when the source claims only 'a trend toward reduced cytotoxicity' relative to a toxic parent and makes no vehicle-relative claim at all. The source figures actually annotate BOTH comparators ('# and * indicates significance against vehicle and ASO2, respectively'), so the vehicle-relative sign is recoverable - it just was not recorded. Fix: make the comparator explicit in effect_vs_control, or add a comparator field. Any oligo whose name encodes a modification of a named parent (PS-n(-), 5'-CP position n, 2'-OMe gap position n) is a candidate. 

4. NO DECLARED DEG-COUNT-TO-GRADE MAPPING, producing inverted grades. Within the same paper (Kuijper), 11 387 DEGs (45% of the 25 124 genes tested) is graded 1 (CMS2129) while 9 385 DEGs is graded 2 (CMS2138). More broadly the lane grades transcriptomic burden inconsistently: 9 and 11 DEGs grade 0 (microglia), 867 splicing events grade 1, 11 387 DEGs grade 1, 9 385 DEGs grade 2. A model trained on this learns a non-monotonic relationship between transcriptome perturbation and severity. Declare an explicit threshold (or normalise DEGs to genes tested) and apply it uniformly across all transcriptomic rows in the dataset. 

5. IN VITRO GRADES 2 AND 3 ARE NOT ANCHORED TO THE RUBRIC. The rubric is written for in vivo/clinical endpoints (degeneration, paralysis, hydrocephalus, dose-limiting toxicity) and has no in vitro mapping, so grades drift. Clearest case: CMS2063 grades a CDKN1A mRNA rise in a neuroblastoma line as 3, outranking the parent oligo's actual cell-death readout at 2 (CMS2060). Elsewhere grade-3 rationales are imported from the matched in vivo mouse study (CMS2069) rather than from the in vitro measurement being graded. Recommend an explicit in vitro annex to the rubric - e.g. cell loss / LDH release above vehicle = 2, with 3 reserved for near-complete culture loss - and re-grade the whole in vitro lane against it. All 40 rows carry 'grade_provisional', so this is expected work, not a surprise. 

6. ENDPOINT_DOMAIN INFLATES THE HIGH-PRIORITY CHRONIC BUCKET. Rows are filed as chronic_neurotoxicity/high_chronic_neurotox on exposures that are not chronic and endpoints that are not toxicity: CMS2078 (3-hour transfection), CMS2063 (72 h), CMS2108 (a disease-phenotype rescue). Since NCATS weights this bucket most heavily, a defensible minimum exposure for 'chronic' (the genuinely chronic rows here are 14-28 d: SCA3, MECP2-duplication, Kotowska-Zimmer, KIF1A) should be declared and applied, and pure efficacy-rescue endpoints should not sit in it.
